question_bank.q: Why do you want to work here / for this company?
question_bank.a: I'm drawn to the company's use of data to drive real commercial decisions, which is where I've focused for the last 4 years. My MMM, pricing and analytics-engineering experience maps closely to the role, and I'm keen to contribute quickly while growing with a strong data team.

question_bank.q: Why are you a good fit for this role?
question_bank.a: I bring 4+ years turning messy commercial data into decisions — MMM and trade-promotion optimisation, forecasting, segmentation and risk analytics — on Python/SQL/PySpark/Azure with Power BI/Tableau, plus recent GenAI/RAG project work. I own problems end to end, from data to deployed model to stakeholder story.
Commercial/marketing analytics (MMM, pricing), end-to-end delivery on Azure, and translating models into clear decisions for non-technical stakeholders.

question_bank.q: What is your biggest weakness / area to develop?
question_bank.a: I'm deepening large-scale cloud data-warehousing beyond Azure (BigQuery/Snowflake); I pick up new tools fast and am actively learning.

question_bank.q: Describe a project you're proud of.
question_bank.a: Marketing Mix Modelling + trade-promotion optimisation for a $1B+ US confectionery portfolio: I built log-log elasticity models in PySpark/Databricks and an optimisation that improved trade-spend efficiency by ~8%, then delivered it to commercial teams via Power BI.

question_bank.q: Where do you see yourself in a few years?
question_bank.a: Growing into a senior data scientist / analytics leader, deep in commercial and marketing-science modelling while mentoring others.

question_bank.q: Are you authorised to work in the UK?
question_bank.a: Yes — I hold a UK Graduate visa and can work now without sponsorship.
Not for UK roles now (Graduate visa). For non-UK roles I would need sponsorship.
Around £45,000, flexible on the overall package and the role.

question_bank.q: When can you start / notice period?
question_bank.a: About one month; I can be flexible.

question_bank.q: Cover letter / anything else you'd like us to know?
question_bank.a: I'm a data scientist with 4+ years in commercial analytics (MMM, pricing, forecasting, segmentation) plus recent GenAI/RAG work, an MSc Data Science (Distinction) and Microsoft certifications. I'd bring immediate, hands-on value and am excited about this role.

voice: First person, warm but professional, concise (2-4 sentences unless more is asked). UK spelling, no em-dashes, no buzzword-stuffing. Always grounded in the real experience above — never invent tools, employers, figures or qualifications. If a question asks about something I lack, be honest and pivot to the closest real, transferable experience.
summary: Data professional with 4+ years across retail, consumer, energy/collections and insurance domains. Core stack Python, SQL, PySpark, R, Azure (Databricks/Data Factory/ML/Synapse), Power BI/Tableau. Differentiator: Marketing Mix Modelling (MMM), trade-promotion optimisation and pricing/commercial analytics. Recent GenAI/RAG/NLP project work during an MSc Data Science (76%, Coventry). Certified: Databricks GenAI Engineer, IBM Data Science, Google Data Analytics, Microsoft PL-300 and AZ-900. Strong on turning models into commercial decisions.
honest_gaps: Azure is my primary, production-evidenced cloud. I have ALSO used Google Cloud (BigQuery, Looker, Looker Studio, Vertex AI) and AWS (SageMaker, S3, Redshift, Glue) hands-on in PERSONAL and ACADEMIC projects — present these as genuine project experience, not enterprise production. Still avoid overclaiming: no large-scale production data-warehouse ownership, no dbt or Snowflake in production, no people-leadership, no heavy deep-learning research.
